edits.target: 3. Choose a method suited to the workbook. Use formulas when the workbook should remain dynamically linked; use a script or spreadsheet library for large, repeated, or structural transformations.
edits.content: 3. Choose a method suited to the workbook. Use formulas when the workbook should remain dynamically linked; use a script or spreadsheet library for large, repeated, or structural transformations. When a script is used, compute target values in Python and write them as literals unless the task explicitly requires a formula—this avoids fragility from array-formula syntax differences, implicit-intersection behavior, or recalculation engine variations. When deleting rows, always iterate from the bottom of the sheet upward so row indices do not shift beneath you.
edits.applicability: All spreadsheet tasks where the agent writes a script (openpyxl/pandas) to modify cell values or delete rows.
edits.non_applicability: Tasks that explicitly require writing Excel formulas for dynamic linkage, or tasks that only read data without structural modifications.
edits.expected_effect: More reliable value writing by avoiding formula recalculation ambiguity, and correct row deletion without index-shift errors.
